items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No files were changed or kept. The only code was throwaway inline `python3 -c` one-liners (e.g. `d=open(...)`, `c=sqli...`, `r`), and they were never saved as a script.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: There is no code change to judge. The reconstructed diff shows "(no changes)". The convention asked for a re-runnable decrypt/extract script, but the agent left only inline one-liners in its shell history.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No code was saved to judge. The inline one-liners hardcode `0x42` and handle no errors, but they rely on `&&` chaining, and the step 2 failure (`cp: cannot stat`) surfaced rather than being swallowed.

items.name: Recovery method is principled
items.evidence: The key came from evidence: `753d44c0` XOR `377f0682` gives 0x42. The agent decrypted the whole file in /tmp, let SQLite replay the WAL, ran `pragma integrity_check` (ok), and checked `count(*)`=11 before writing the JSON.

items.name: Original evidence preserved before in-place repair
items.name_zh: 原地修复前保留原始文件
items.evidence: The first modifying command was `cp main.db /tmp/main.db.orig && cp main.db-wal /tmp/main.db-wal.orig`, run before any decrypt or read-write open. The agent tested on a copy in /tmp/w and decrypted the final WAL from the .orig backup.
